ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An adjective is a word that (1 mark)
   A. shows an action
   B. names a person
   C. describes a noun
   D. joins sentences

2. About how long is a Grade 4 narrative composition? (1 mark)
   A. 5 words
   B. 10 words
   C. 60 to 80 words
   D. 1000 words

3. A story that you heard on the radio and write in your own words is (1 mark)
   A. a retelling
   B. a map
   C. a menu
   D. a receipt

4. Quantifiers: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. I do not have some money.
   B. I do not have any money.
   C. I do not have many money.
   D. I do not any have money.

5. Why do two learners write different stories from the same pictures? (1 mark)
   A. Each writer uses different words and ideas
   B. One is always wrong
   C. The pictures are blank
   D. They copy each other

6. Which word has the /j/ sound although it begins with the letter u? (1 mark)
   A. umbrella
   B. under
   C. uncle
   D. use

7. Which word has the /ʤ/ sound at the beginning? (1 mark)
   A. giraffe
   B. yellow
   C. treasure
   D. chair

8. What is a rhyme? (1 mark)
   A. Words with the same meaning
   B. Words that end with the same sound
   C. Words with opposite meanings
   D. Words that start with the same letter

9. How do you make the question form of 'She is reading'? (1 mark)
   A. Is reading she?
   B. She is reading?
   C. Is she reading?
   D. Does she reading?

10. When do we write the word 'I' as a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. Only at the start of a sentence
   B. Never
   C. Only in names
   D. Always

11. Which sentence has the right capital letters and full stop? (1 mark)
   A. akinyi lives near River Nzoia!
   B. akinyi lives near river nzoia
   C. Akinyi lives near River Nzoia.
   D. Akinyi lives near river nzoia,

12. What does 'indigenous' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very expensive
   B. Grown in a factory
   C. Belonging naturally to a place
   D. Damaged by pests

13. What is reader's theatre? (1 mark)
   A. Silent reading
   B. Acting a play with full costumes
   C. Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   D. Copying a script

14. What is rhythm in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. The title of the poem
   B. The beat in the words
   C. The name of the poet
   D. The number of pages

15. Which word helps to show the order of events? (1 mark)
   A. farm
   B. heavy
   C. green
   D. suddenly

16. Which of these can spread HIV? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing a plate of food
   B. Playing football together
   C. Sharing a razor blade
   D. Hugging a friend

17. Which is an adverb of time meaning 'not at any time'? (1 mark)
   A. usually
   B. never
   C. often
   D. sometimes

18. Which adverb has the same form as its adjective? (1 mark)
   A. slowly
   B. hard
   C. gently
   D. quickly

19. Which sentence is punctuated correctly? (1 mark)
   A. We bought rice, beans, and, maize.
   B. We bought rice, beans and maize.
   C. We bought, rice beans and maize.
   D. We bought rice beans and maize.

20. What is the job of a comma? (1 mark)
   A. To show a question
   B. To end a sentence
   C. To show strong feeling
   D. To show a short pause and to separate items

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write two similes to describe a tractor and a hot day. (2 marks)

22. Write a sentence that has an adverb of manner, an adverb of time and an adverb of place. (3 marks)

23. State two habits of a good listener. (2 marks)

24. Change to negative statements: (a) She sells eggs. (b) They picked coffee. (4 marks)

25. What kind of person is Baraka? Give one reason from the story. (3 marks)

26. Change these adjectives into adverbs: gentle, angry, quick. (3 marks)

27. List three steps to follow before writing a pictorial composition. (3 marks)

28. Explain the difference between a common noun and a proper noun. Give one example of each. (3 marks)

29. Write two words that contain /ɛə/, two that begin with /j/ and one that has /ʒ/. (5 marks)

30. Write two similes about food. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #2 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — describes a noun
   Adjectives describe nouns.

2. C — 60 to 80 words
   The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

3. A — a retelling
   You tell the same story in new words.

4. B — I do not have any money.
   Use any in negative sentences.

5. A — Each writer uses different words and ideas
   Each writer has a different voice.

6. D — use
   'Use' is said 'yooz', beginning with /j/.

7. A — giraffe
   In 'giraffe' the g says /ʤ/.

8. B — Words that end with the same sound
   'Wide' and 'ride' rhyme.

9. C — Is she reading?
   Put is before the subject.

10. D — Always
   'I' is always a capital.

11. C — Akinyi lives near River Nzoia.
   Names and the first word begin with capitals, and the statement ends with a full stop.

12. C — Belonging naturally to a place
   Indigenous plants and animals are native to a place.

13. C — Reading parts from a script with only your voice, without costumes or sets
   Reader's theatre uses voices only.

14. B — The beat in the words
   Rhythm is the pattern of beats.

15. D — suddenly
   'Suddenly' is a time word.

16. C — Sharing a razor blade
   HIV can pass through blood, so razor blades must never be shared.

17. B — never
   'Never' means at no time.

18. B — hard
   'He works hard' uses hard as an adverb.

19. B — We bought rice, beans and maize.
   Commas separate items in a list and 'and' comes before the last.

20. D — To show a short pause and to separate items
   Commas mark short pauses and separate list items.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: For example: The tractor roared like a lion. The day was as hot as a burning coal.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each suitable simile.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example: Yesterday the children played happily outside.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct adverb.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look at the speaker and keep quiet until the speaker has finished a whole idea. Nodding to show you follow is also correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct habit.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: (a) She doesn't sell eggs. (b) They didn't pick coffee.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks each: 1 for the correct helping verb, 1 for the base form of the main verb.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: He is kind and brave. He went to talk to Omondi, explained the facts and invited him to play.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a quality and 2 for the evidence.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: gently, angrily, quickly
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Look at all the pictures, put them in order, ask who, where and what, make notes, think of a title.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: A common noun is a general name such as 'town'. A proper noun is the special name of one person, place or thing, such as 'Kisumu', and begins with a capital letter.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 for both examples.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: /ɛə/: chair, care. /j/: yellow, young. /ʒ/: television.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: The bread was as soft as a pillow. The juice was as sweet as honey.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
